stem: Bilal needs an enlarged view of a tiny circuit mark and also wants parallel torch rays to meet at one bright point.

options.text: A concave mirror held close for enlarged viewing, and a concave mirror facing parallel rays for light concentration.
A plane mirror for both enlarged viewing and light concentration.
A convex mirror held close for an enlarged view of the tiny mark.

parts.text: Why does a concave mirror help with the tiny circuit mark when held close?

part_answers.answer: It can give an enlarged image of a nearby object.

teacher.key_rationale: Concave mirrors can enlarge nearby objects and can converge parallel light to a point. Plane and convex mirrors do not match both of those needs.
